meta.topic: 线性代数：特征值、相似与对角化、实对称矩阵、若尔当标准型、最小多项式、λ-矩阵、正规矩阵

zh: 设 $A$ 是 $n$ 阶方阵，$\alpha\neq0$。由 $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$ 移项得 $(\lambda E-A)\alpha=0$，这是以 $\alpha$ 为未知量的 $n$ 元齐次方程组。它有非零解当且仅当系数矩阵不可逆，即 $$\det(\lambda E-A)=0.$$ 左端记为 $f_A(\lambda)$，展开后是 $\lambda$ 的 $n$ 次首一多项式，称为特征多项式。因此在复数域上按代数重数恰有 $n$ 个根，它们就是 $A$ 的全部特征值；实矩阵的复特征值成共轭对出现。

以 $2\times2$ 为例，$A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ 时 $$\begin{aligned}f_A(\lambda)&=(\lambda-a)(\lambda-d)-bc\\&=\lambda^2-(a+d)\lambda+(ad-bc).\end{aligned}$$ 一般地 $f_A(\lambda)=\lambda^n-\operatorname{tr}(A)\lambda^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^n\det A$。由韦达定理，$$\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i=\operatorname{tr}(A),\qquad \prod_{i=1}^n\lambda_i=\det A.$$ 这两条是算完特征值后的免费校验；特别地 $\det A=0$ 当且仅当 $0$ 是特征值。

固定特征值 $\lambda_0$，其特征子空间为 $V_{\lambda_0}=\ker(\lambda_0E-A)$，几何重数 $g=\dim V_{\lambda_0}=n-r(\lambda_0E-A)$。取 $V_{\lambda_0}$ 的一组基 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_g$，扩充为全空间的基 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_g,\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{n-g}$。由于 $A\alpha_i=\lambda_0\alpha_i$，$A$ 在这组基下的矩阵为分块上三角 $$\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_0E_g&*\\0&B\end{pmatrix},$$ 故 $f_A(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^g\det(\lambda E_{n-g}-B)$。于是 $\lambda_0$ 的代数重数 $m\ge g$：代数重数总不小于几何重数。

不同特征值的特征向量线性无关。设 $A\alpha_i=\lambda_i\alpha_i$，$\alpha_i
eq0$，$\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$ 两两不同，且 $\sum_{i=1}^s c_i\alpha_i=0$。对每个 $k$，用 $\prod_{j
eq k}(A-\lambda_jE)$ 作用。含 $i
eq k$ 的项被因子 $(A-\lambda_iE)$ 杀死，只剩 $$c_k\prod_{j
eq k}(\lambda_k-\lambda_j)\,\alpha_k=0.$$ 系数与 $\alpha_k$ 都非零，故 $c_k=0$；对 $k=1,\dots,s$ 都成立，所以这些特征向量线性无关。

例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$。$f_A(\lambda)=(\lambda-2)(\lambda-1)$，特征值为 $2,1$。$\lambda=2$ 时 $(2E-A)x=0$ 给出 $x_2=0$，取 $\alpha_1=(1,0)^T$；$\lambda=1$ 时 $(E-A)x=0$ 给出 $x_1+x_2=0$，取 $\alpha_2=(1,-1)^T$。校验：$\operatorname{tr}(A)=3=2+1$，$\det A=2=2\cdot1$。而 $A(1,1)^T=(3,1)^T$ 与 $(1,1)^T$ 不成比例，故 $(1,1)^T$ 不是特征向量。

三个边界不能忽略。其一，零向量不是特征向量，因为 $A0=\lambda0$ 对一切 $\lambda$ 成立。其二，不同特征值的特征向量之和一般不是特征向量：$A(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)=\lambda_1\alpha_1+\lambda_2\alpha_2$，当 $\lambda_1\neq\lambda_2$ 时提不出公共倍数。其三，若 $A$ 可逆（等价于所有特征值非零），则 $A^{-1}\alpha=\lambda^{-1}\alpha$，且 $A^k\alpha=\lambda^k\alpha$；$\lambda=0$ 时 $A$ 不可逆，$A^{-1}$ 不存在。
en: Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix and $\alpha\neq0$. Rewriting $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$ as $(\lambda E-A)\alpha=0$ gives a homogeneous system of $n$ equations in the unknown $\alpha$. It has a nonzero solution exactly when the coefficient matrix is singular, that is, $$\det(\lambda E-A)=0.$$ The left side, denoted $f_A(\lambda)$, is a monic polynomial of degree $n$, the characteristic polynomial. Hence over $\mathbb{C}$ it has exactly $n$ roots counted with algebraic multiplicity, and these are precisely the eigenvalues of $A$; for a real matrix, nonreal eigenvalues occur in conjugate pairs.

For a $2\times2$ example, if $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, then $$\begin{aligned}f_A(\lambda)&=(\lambda-a)(\lambda-d)-bc\\&=\lambda^2-(a+d)\lambda+(ad-bc).\end{aligned}$$ In general $f_A(\lambda)=\lambda^n-\operatorname{tr}(A)\lambda^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^n\det A$. By Vieta's formulas, $$\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i=\operatorname{tr}(A),\qquad \prod_{i=1}^n\lambda_i=\det A.$$ These identities are free checks after computing the eigenvalues; in particular $\det A=0$ if and only if $0$ is an eigenvalue.

Fix an eigenvalue $\lambda_0$. Its eigenspace is $V_{\lambda_0}=\ker(\lambda_0E-A)$, with geometric multiplicity $g=\dim V_{\lambda_0}=n-r(\lambda_0E-A)$. Choose a basis $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_g$ of $V_{\lambda_0}$ and extend it to a basis $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_g,\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{n-g}$ of the whole space. Since $A\alpha_i=\lambda_0\alpha_i$, the matrix of $A$ in this basis is block upper triangular $$\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_0E_g&*\\0&B\end{pmatrix},$$ so $f_A(\lambda)=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^g\det(\lambda E_{n-g}-B)$. Therefore the algebraic multiplicity $m$ of $\lambda_0$ satisfies $m\ge g$: the algebraic multiplicity is always at least the geometric one.

Eigenvectors belonging to distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent. Let $A\alpha_i=\lambda_i\alpha_i$ with $\alpha_i
eq0$ and pairwise distinct $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$, and suppose $\sum_{i=1}^s c_i\alpha_i=0$. For each $k$, apply $\prod_{j
eq k}(A-\lambda_jE)$. Every term with $i
eq k$ is killed by the factor $(A-\lambda_iE)$, leaving only $$c_k\prod_{j
eq k}(\lambda_k-\lambda_j)\,\alpha_k=0.$$ Both the coefficient and $\alpha_k$ are nonzero, so $c_k=0$; this holds for every $k$, hence the eigenvectors are linearly independent.

Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Then $f_A(\lambda)=(\lambda-2)(\lambda-1)$, so the eigenvalues are $2$ and $1$. For $\lambda=2$, the system $(2E-A)x=0$ gives $x_2=0$, so take $\alpha_1=(1,0)^T$; for $\lambda=1$, $(E-A)x=0$ gives $x_1+x_2=0$, so take $\alpha_2=(1,-1)^T$. Checks: $\operatorname{tr}(A)=3=2+1$ and $\det A=2=2\cdot1$. On the other hand, $A(1,1)^T=(3,1)^T$ is not proportional to $(1,1)^T$, so $(1,1)^T$ is not an eigenvector.

Three boundary cases matter. First, the zero vector is not an eigenvector, since $A0=\lambda0$ holds for every $\lambda$. Second, a sum of eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues is generally not an eigenvector: $A(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)=\lambda_1\alpha_1+\lambda_2\alpha_2$ has no common factor when $\lambda_1\neq\lambda_2$. Third, if $A$ is invertible (equivalently, all eigenvalues are nonzero), then $A^{-1}\alpha=\lambda^{-1}\alpha$ and $A^k\alpha=\lambda^k\alpha$; when $\lambda=0$, $A$ is singular and $A^{-1}$ does not exist.

zh: 设 $A,B$ 为 $n$ 阶方阵。若存在可逆矩阵 $P$ 使 $B=P^{-1}AP$，称 $A$ 与 $B$ 相似。相似是等价关系：自反取 $P=E$，对称取 $P^{-1}$，传递把两个过渡矩阵相乘。几何上，$A$ 与 $B$ 是同一个线性变换在两组基下的矩阵，$P$ 是两组基之间的过渡矩阵；因此相似就是「换基看同一个变换」。

相似不变量：$$\begin{aligned}f_B(\lambda)&=\det(\lambda E-P^{-1}AP)\\&=\det\bigl(P^{-1}(\lambda E-A)P\bigr)\\&=\det(P^{-1})f_A(\lambda)\det P=f_A(\lambda).\end{aligned}$$ 所以相似矩阵有相同的特征多项式、特征值（含重数）、迹、行列式与秩。反过来不成立：$E$ 与 $J=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 的特征多项式都是 $(\lambda-1)^2$，但 $E$ 只相似于自己，而 $J\neq E$，故二者不相似。

可对角化的含义：$A=P\Lambda P^{-1}$，$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$，等价于 $AP=P\Lambda$。比较第 $i$ 列得 $Ap_i=\lambda_ip_i$。$P$ 可逆保证 $p_1,\dots,p_n$ 线性无关且非零，所以它们是一组特征向量基。反之，若 $A$ 有 $n$ 个线性无关的特征向量 $p_i$，令 $P=(p_1,\dots,p_n)$，则 $AP=P\Lambda$，即 $P^{-1}AP=\Lambda$。因此 $$A\ \text{可对角化}\iff A\ \text{有}\ n\ \text{个线性无关的特征向量}.$$ 列的顺序必须与对角元的顺序一致。

重数判据：设互异特征值为 $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$，代数重数 $m_i$，几何重数 $g_i=n-r(\lambda_iE-A)$。对每个 $\lambda_i$，取其特征子空间的一组基并扩充为全空间的基，可知 $A$ 的矩阵呈分块上三角，故 $g_i\le m_i$。不同特征值的特征子空间之和是直和，且 $\sum m_i=n$。于是 $$\begin{aligned}A\ \text{可对角化}&\iff \sum_{i=1}^s g_i=n\\&\iff g_i=m_i\quad(i=1,\dots,s).\end{aligned}$$ 理由：$\sum g_i=n$ 说明这些特征子空间的基拼成 $n$ 个线性无关特征向量；而 $\sum g_i\le\sum m_i=n$，取等当且仅当每一项都取等。

$n$ 个互异特征值是可对角化的充分条件：此时每个 $m_i=1$，而特征值必有非零特征向量，故 $g_i\ge1$，于是 $g_i=m_i=1$。它不是必要条件：$E_n$ 只有特征值 $1$，$m_1=n$，但 $g_1=n$，本身已是对角阵。例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$，$f_A=(\lambda-4)(\lambda-2)$，取 $p_1=(1,-1)^T$、$p_2=(1,1)^T$，则 $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$ 可逆，且 $P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}(4,2)$。

不可对角化的典型例子：$J=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$，$f_J=(\lambda-1)^2$，代数重数 $m_1=2$，但 $g_1=2-r(J-E)=2-1=1$，故不可对角化。这也说明特征值相同远弱于相似。可对角化时，幂与多项式有简单公式：$$A^k=P\Lambda^kP^{-1},\qquad f(A)=Pf(\Lambda)P^{-1};$$ 若 $A$ 可逆（所有 $\lambda_i\neq0$），还有 $A^{-1}=P\Lambda^{-1}P^{-1}$。这把矩阵乘法降为对角元的运算。
en: Let $A,B$ be $n\times n$ matrices. If $B=P^{-1}AP$ for some invertible $P$, then $A$ and $B$ are similar. Similarity is an equivalence relation: reflexivity uses $P=E$, symmetry uses $P^{-1}$, and transitivity multiplies the two transition matrices. Geometrically, $A$ and $B$ are matrices of the same linear transformation in two bases, with $P$ the transition matrix; similarity means viewing one transformation from two angles.

Similarity invariants: $$\begin{aligned}f_B(\lambda)&=\det(\lambda E-P^{-1}AP)\\&=\det\bigl(P^{-1}(\lambda E-A)P\bigr)\\&=\det(P^{-1})f_A(\lambda)\det P=f_A(\lambda).\end{aligned}$$ Thus similar matrices share the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues with multiplicities, trace, determinant and rank. The converse fails: $E$ and $J=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ both have characteristic polynomial $(\lambda-1)^2$, but $E$ is similar only to itself and $J\neq E$, so they are not similar.

Diagonalizability: $A=P\Lambda P^{-1}$ with $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is equivalent to $AP=P\Lambda$. Comparing the $i$-th columns gives $Ap_i=\lambda_ip_i$. Since $P$ is invertible, $p_1,\dots,p_n$ are linearly independent and nonzero, hence form an eigenvector basis. Conversely, if $A$ has $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors $p_i$, set $P=(p_1,\dots,p_n)$; then $AP=P\Lambda$, i.e. $P^{-1}AP=\Lambda$. Therefore $$A\ \text{is diagonalizable}\iff A\ \text{has}\ n\ \text{linearly independent eigenvectors}.$$ The order of the columns must match the order of the diagonal entries.

Multiplicity criterion: let $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$ be the distinct eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicities $m_i$ and geometric multiplicities $g_i=n-r(\lambda_iE-A)$. For each $\lambda_i$, take a basis of its eigenspace and extend it to a basis of the whole space; the matrix of $A$ becomes block upper triangular, so $g_i\le m_i$. Eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues are independent, so their sum is direct, and $\sum m_i=n$. Hence $$\begin{aligned}A\ \text{is diagonalizable}&\iff \sum_{i=1}^s g_i=n\\&\iff g_i=m_i\quad(i=1,\dots,s).\end{aligned}$$ Indeed, $\sum g_i=n$ means the bases of the eigenspaces combine into $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors; since $\sum g_i\le\sum m_i=n$, equality holds exactly when every term is equal.

Having $n$ distinct eigenvalues is sufficient for diagonalizability: then $m_i=1$, while every eigenvalue has a nonzero eigenvector, so $g_i\ge1$ and hence $g_i=m_i=1$. It is not necessary: $E_n$ has only the eigenvalue $1$ with $m_1=n$, but $g_1=n$, and it is already diagonal. Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$ has $f_A=(\lambda-4)(\lambda-2)$; taking $p_1=(1,-1)^T$ and $p_2=(1,1)^T$, the matrix $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$ is invertible and $P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}(4,2)$.

A typical non-diagonalizable matrix is $J=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$: $f_J=(\lambda-1)^2$, so the algebraic multiplicity is $m_1=2$, but $g_1=2-r(J-E)=2-1=1$, hence $J$ is not diagonalizable. This also shows that equal eigenvalues are far weaker than similarity. When $A$ is diagonalizable, powers and polynomials simplify: $$A^k=P\Lambda^kP^{-1},\qquad f(A)=Pf(\Lambda)P^{-1};$$ if $A$ is invertible (all $\lambda_i\neq0$), then also $A^{-1}=P\Lambda^{-1}P^{-1}$. This reduces matrix multiplication to operations on diagonal entries.

zh: 设 $A\in M_n(\mathbb{R})$，$A^T=A$。把 $A$ 看作复矩阵，设 $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$，$\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$，并用复内积 $(\alpha,\beta)=\beta^H\alpha$。由 $A$ 实对称得 $A^H=A$，于是 $$\lambda\|\alpha\|^2=(A\alpha,\alpha)=\alpha^HA\alpha=(\alpha,A\alpha)=\bar\lambda\|\alpha\|^2.$$ 因为 $\|\alpha\|^2>0$，所以 $\lambda=\bar\lambda$，即实对称矩阵的特征值全为实数。

不同特征值的特征向量正交。设 $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$，$A eta=\mu eta$，$\lambda
eq\mu$，$\alpha, eta
eq0$；由第 1 步 $\lambda,\mu$ 为实数，故可取实特征向量。对实向量用 $(x,y)=y^Tx$，由 $A^T=A$ 得 $$(A\alpha, eta)= eta^TA\alpha=(A eta)^T\alpha=(\alpha,A eta).$$ 左端为 $\lambda(\alpha, eta)$，右端为 $\mu(\alpha, eta)$，故 $(\lambda-\mu)(\alpha, eta)=0$。由于 $\lambda
eq\mu$，只能 $(\alpha, eta)=0$。

存在性用对维数归纳。$n=1$ 显然。设 $n\ge2$，特征多项式在 $\mathbb{C}$ 上有根，由第 1 步该根为实数，取单位实特征向量 $q_1$，$Aq_1=\lambda_1q_1$。令 $W=q_1^\perp=\{x:(x,q_1)=0\}$，则 $\dim W=n-1$。若 $x\in W$，则 $$(Ax,q_1)=(x,Aq_1)=\lambda_1(x,q_1)=0,$$ 故 $Ax\in W$，即 $W$ 是 $A$-不变子空间。限制 $A|_W$ 仍是对称的，由归纳假设 $W$ 有由 $A$ 的特征向量组成的标准正交基 $q_2,\dots,q_n$。

于是 $q_1,\dots,q_n$ 是 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的标准正交基，且 $Aq_i=\lambda_iq_i$。令 $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)$，则 $Q^TQ=E$，$AQ=Q\Lambda$，其中 $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$，所以 $$Q^TAQ=Q^{-1}AQ=\Lambda.$$ 因为 $Q^{-1}=Q^T$，同一个变换既是相似又是合同；对角元全为实数。这就是实对称矩阵的正交对角化。

上述构造给出 $n$ 个线性无关特征向量，因此每个特征值的几何重数都等于代数重数：若某个 $g_i<m_i$，则由 $\sum g_i=n=\sum m_i$ 与 $g_i\le m_i$ 会推出矛盾。等价地，$k$ 重特征值恰有 $k$ 维特征子空间。写成谱分解：$$A=Q\Lambda Q^T=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_iq_iq_i^T,$$ 其中 $q_iq_i^T$ 是到 $\operatorname{span}(q_i)$ 的正交投影，满足 $(q_iq_i^T)^2=q_iq_i^T$、$q_iq_i^Tq_jq_j^T=0\ (i\neq j)$ 以及 $\sum_iq_iq_i^T=E$。

逆命题：若存在正交矩阵 $Q$ 使 $Q^TAQ=\Lambda$ 为对角阵，则 $A=Q\Lambda Q^T$，从而 $$A^T=Q\Lambda^TQ^T=Q\Lambda Q^T=A,$$ 故 $A$ 实对称。因此「可正交对角化」是实对称矩阵的充分必要条件。例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$，特征值 $3,1$，单位特征向量 $q_1=(1,1)^T/\sqrt2$、$q_2=(1,-1)^T/\sqrt2$，令 $Q=(q_1,q_2)$，则 $Q^TAQ=\operatorname{diag}(3,1)$。注意一般可对角化矩阵未必能正交对角化，例如 $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ 特征值互异却不对称。
en: Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb{R})$ with $A^T=A$. Regard $A$ as a complex matrix and let $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$, using the complex inner product $(\alpha,\beta)=\beta^H\alpha$. Since $A$ is real symmetric, $A^H=A$, and hence $$\lambda\|\alpha\|^2=(A\alpha,\alpha)=\alpha^HA\alpha=(\alpha,A\alpha)=\bar\lambda\|\alpha\|^2.$$ Because $\|\alpha\|^2>0$, it follows that $\lambda=\bar\lambda$: every eigenvalue of a real symmetric matrix is real.

Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal. Let $A\alpha=\lambda\alpha$ and $A eta=\mu eta$ with $\lambda
eq\mu$ and $\alpha, eta
eq0$; by Step 1, $\lambda,\mu$ are real, so real eigenvectors may be chosen. For real vectors use $(x,y)=y^Tx$; from $A^T=A$, $$(A\alpha, eta)= eta^TA\alpha=(A eta)^T\alpha=(\alpha,A eta).$$ The left side is $\lambda(\alpha, eta)$ and the right side is $\mu(\alpha, eta)$, so $(\lambda-\mu)(\alpha, eta)=0$. Since $\lambda
eq\mu$, we get $(\alpha, eta)=0$.

Existence is proved by induction on the dimension. The case $n=1$ is clear. For $n\ge2$, the characteristic polynomial has a complex root, which is real by Step 1; choose a unit real eigenvector $q_1$ with $Aq_1=\lambda_1q_1$. Let $W=q_1^\perp=\{x:(x,q_1)=0\}$, so $\dim W=n-1$. If $x\in W$, then $$(Ax,q_1)=(x,Aq_1)=\lambda_1(x,q_1)=0,$$ so $Ax\in W$; thus $W$ is $A$-invariant. The restriction $A|_W$ is still symmetric, and by induction $W$ has an orthonormal basis $q_2,\dots,q_n$ consisting of eigenvectors of $A$.

Therefore $q_1,\dots,q_n$ is an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $Aq_i=\lambda_iq_i$. Let $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)$; then $Q^TQ=E$ and $AQ=Q\Lambda$, where $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$, so $$Q^TAQ=Q^{-1}AQ=\Lambda.$$ Since $Q^{-1}=Q^T$, the same transformation is both a similarity and a congruence; all diagonal entries are real. This is orthogonal diagonalization of a real symmetric matrix.

The construction yields $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors, so every geometric multiplicity equals the corresponding algebraic multiplicity: if some $g_i<m_i$, then $\sum g_i=n=\sum m_i$ together with $g_i\le m_i$ would give a contradiction. Equivalently, an eigenvalue of multiplicity $k$ has a $k$-dimensional eigenspace. In spectral form, $$A=Q\Lambda Q^T=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_iq_iq_i^T,$$ where $q_iq_i^T$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(q_i)$, with $(q_iq_i^T)^2=q_iq_i^T$, $q_iq_i^Tq_jq_j^T=0$ for $i\neq j$, and $\sum_iq_iq_i^T=E$.

Converse: if an orthogonal $Q$ makes $Q^TAQ=\Lambda$ diagonal, then $A=Q\Lambda Q^T$, so $$A^T=Q\Lambda^TQ^T=Q\Lambda Q^T=A,$$ and $A$ is real symmetric. Thus, for real matrices, orthogonal diagonalizability is equivalent to symmetry. Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ has eigenvalues $3,1$ and unit eigenvectors $q_1=(1,1)^T/\sqrt2$, $q_2=(1,-1)^T/\sqrt2$; with $Q=(q_1,q_2)$, $Q^TAQ=\operatorname{diag}(3,1)$. Note that a general diagonalizable matrix need not be orthogonally diagonalizable: $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ has distinct eigenvalues but is not symmetric.

zh: 对角化失败的根源是特征向量不够。$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ 的特征多项式为 $(\lambda-1)^2$，但 $r(A-E)=1$，几何重数 $2-1=1<2$，凑不齐两个线性无关特征向量。若尔当块把「对角」放宽为「准对角」：$$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E_k+N_k,$$ 其中 $N_k$ 的上副对角线全为 $1$、其余为 $0$。直接计算可知 $N_k^j$ 把 $1$ 移到第 $j$ 条上副对角线，故 $N_k^k=O$，且 $j<k$ 时 $N_k^j\neq O$。

若尔当标准型定理：设 $A$ 是 $n$ 阶复矩阵，则存在可逆 $P$ 使 $$P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),$$ 且 $k_1+\cdots+k_r=n$；不计块的排列次序时 $J$ 唯一。存在性思路：对每个互异特征值 $\lambda$，广义特征子空间 $G_\lambda=\ker((A-\lambda E)^n)$ 是 $A$-不变的，且 $\mathbb{C}^n=\oplus_\lambda G_\lambda$；在 $G_\lambda$ 上 $A-\lambda E$ 幂零，幂零算子的循环链分解给出若干块 $J_k(\lambda)$。在实数域上，若特征值不全为实，需用复过渡矩阵，或改用含 $2\times2$ 旋转—伸缩块的实若尔当形。

链与矩阵：若 $p_1,\dots,p_k$ 满足 $$(A-\lambda E)p_1=0,\qquad (A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j\ (1\le j<k),$$ 且 $p_1\ne0$，令 $p_0=0$，则 $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$。于是 $$A(p_1,\dots,p_k)=(p_1,\dots,p_k)J_k(\lambda):$$ 第 $1$ 列给出 $Ap_1=\lambda p_1$，第 $j$ 列给出 $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$，正好是对角元 $\lambda$ 与上副对角线 $1$。这些 $p_j$ 线性无关：若相关，取最小的 $j$ 使 $p_j$ 可由 $p_1,\dots,p_{j-1}$ 表示，作用 $(A-\lambda E)^{j-1}$ 得 $p_1=0$，与 $p_1\ne0$ 矛盾。

块数公式：在若尔当形 $J$ 中，每个 $k$ 阶块满足 $J_k(\lambda)-\lambda E=N_k$，其核为 $\operatorname{span}(e_1)$，一维；特征值不同的块 $J_k(\mu)-\lambda E$（$\mu\neq\lambda$）可逆。因此 $$\dim\ker(J-\lambda E)=\lambda\ \text{的若尔当块个数}.$$ 相似保持核的维数，故 $$\#\{\lambda\ \text{的块}\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=g_\lambda,$$ 即块数等于几何重数。又 $f_J(\lambda')=\prod_i(\lambda'-\lambda_i)^{k_i}$，故各块阶数之和等于 $\lambda$ 的代数重数；块的总数等于线性无关特征向量的总数。

可对角化判据：$$A\ \text{可对角化}\iff\text{所有若尔当块为 }1\text{ 阶}\iff g_\lambda=m_\lambda\ (\forall\lambda).$$ 特别地，$n$ 个互异特征值使 $m_\lambda=1$，而 $g_\lambda\ge1$，故必可对角化。例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$，$f_A=(\lambda-2)^2$，$r(A-2E)=1$，故 $\lambda=2$ 的块数为 $2-1=1$，只能是一个 $2$ 阶块 $J_2(2)$。取 $p_1=(1,1)^T$ 解 $(A-2E)p_1=0$，$(A-2E)(1,0)^T=(1,1)^T$，取 $p_2=(1,0)^T$；令 $P=(p_1,p_2)$，则 $AP=PJ_2(2)$。

幂与指数：$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E+N$，$N^k=O$，且 $\lambda E$ 与 $N$ 交换，故二项式展开有效。对 $m\ge k$，$$J_k(\lambda)^m=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{m}{i}\lambda^{m-i}N^i,$$ 而 $$e^{tJ_k(\lambda)}=e^{\lambda t}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{t^i}{i!}N^i.$$ 于是 $A^m=PJ^mP^{-1}$、$e^{tA}=Pe^{tJ}P^{-1}$；指数中出现 $t^ie^{\lambda t}$ 型项，正是不可对角化时 $\dot x=Ax$ 解的特征。注意这些公式依赖复若尔当形；实矩阵若需实运算，应使用实若尔当形。
en: The failure of diagonalization comes from too few eigenvectors. For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, the characteristic polynomial is $(\lambda-1)^2$, but $r(A-E)=1$, so the geometric multiplicity is $2-1=1<2$ and there are not two independent eigenvectors. A Jordan block relaxes 'diagonal' to 'almost diagonal': $$J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E_k+N_k,$$ where $N_k$ has $1$'s on the superdiagonal and $0$'s elsewhere. A direct computation shows that $N_k^j$ moves the $1$'s to the $j$-th superdiagonal, so $N_k^k=O$ and $N_k^j\neq O$ for $j<k$.

Jordan normal form theorem: for every $n\times n$ complex matrix $A$ there is an invertible $P$ with $$P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(J_{k_1}(\lambda_1),\dots,J_{k_r}(\lambda_r)\bigr),$$ where $k_1+\cdots+k_r=n$; the form is unique up to the order of the blocks. Idea of existence: for each distinct eigenvalue $\lambda$, the generalized eigenspace $G_\lambda=\ker((A-\lambda E)^n)$ is $A$-invariant and $\mathbb{C}^n=\oplus_\lambda G_\lambda$; on $G_\lambda$ the operator $A-\lambda E$ is nilpotent, and the cyclic-chain decomposition of a nilpotent operator yields blocks $J_k(\lambda)$. Over $\mathbb{R}$, if not all eigenvalues are real, one needs a complex transition matrix or a real Jordan form with $2\times2$ rotation-dilation blocks.

Chains and matrices: if $p_1,\dots,p_k$ satisfy $$(A-\lambda E)p_1=0,\qquad (A-\lambda E)p_{j+1}=p_j\ (1\le j<k),$$ and $p_1\ne0$, then with $p_0=0$ we have $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$. Hence $$A(p_1,\dots,p_k)=(p_1,\dots,p_k)J_k(\lambda):$$ the first column gives $Ap_1=\lambda p_1$, and the $j$-th column gives $Ap_j=\lambda p_j+p_{j-1}$, exactly the diagonal $\lambda$ and superdiagonal $1$. The $p_j$ are linearly independent: if they were dependent, take the least $j$ with $p_j$ in the span of $p_1,\dots,p_{j-1}$ and apply $(A-\lambda E)^{j-1}$ to get $p_1=0$, contradicting $p_1\ne0$.

Counting blocks: in a Jordan form $J$, each block satisfies $J_k(\lambda)-\lambda E=N_k$, whose kernel is $\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, one-dimensional; a block $J_k(\mu)-\lambda E$ with $\mu\neq\lambda$ is invertible. Therefore $$\dim\ker(J-\lambda E)=\text{the number of Jordan blocks of }\lambda.$$ Similarity preserves kernel dimension, so $$\#\{\text{blocks of }\lambda\}=n-r(\lambda E-A)=g_\lambda,$$ the geometric multiplicity. Also $f_J(\lambda')=\prod_i(\lambda'-\lambda_i)^{k_i}$, so the block sizes sum to the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$, and the total number of blocks equals the number of linearly independent eigenvectors.

Diagonalizability criterion: $$A\ \text{is diagonalizable}\iff\text{all Jordan blocks have order }1\iff g_\lambda=m_\lambda\ (\forall\lambda).$$ In particular, $n$ distinct eigenvalues give $m_\lambda=1$ while $g_\lambda\ge1$, so diagonalizability is automatic. Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has $f_A=(\lambda-2)^2$ and $r(A-2E)=1$, so the number of blocks for $\lambda=2$ is $2-1=1$ and the only possibility is one block $J_2(2)$. Take $p_1=(1,1)^T$ solving $(A-2E)p_1=0$; since $(A-2E)(1,0)^T=(1,1)^T$, take $p_2=(1,0)^T$. With $P=(p_1,p_2)$, $AP=PJ_2(2)$.

Powers and exponentials: $J_k(\lambda)=\lambda E+N$ with $N^k=O$, and $\lambda E$ commutes with $N$, so the binomial expansion is valid. For $m\ge k$, $$J_k(\lambda)^m=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{m}{i}\lambda^{m-i}N^i,$$ while $$e^{tJ_k(\lambda)}=e^{\lambda t}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{t^i}{i!}N^i.$$ Hence $A^m=PJ^mP^{-1}$ and $e^{tA}=Pe^{tJ}P^{-1}$; the exponential contains terms $t^ie^{\lambda t}$, the hallmark of non-diagonalizable systems $\dot x=Ax$. These formulas rely on the complex Jordan form; for real matrices requiring real arithmetic, use the real Jordan form.

zh: 设 $A\in M_n(\mathbb{K})$。若非零多项式 $f$ 满足 $f(A)=O$，称 $f$ 为 $A$ 的零化多项式。由 Cayley–Hamilton 定理，特征多项式 $f_A$ 零化 $A$，故零化多项式集合非空。取其中次数最低的首一多项式，记为 $m_A$，称为最小多项式。唯一性：若首一多项式 $m_1,m_2$ 都次数最低且 $m_1\neq m_2$，则 $m_1-m_2$ 首项相消，是非零、次数更低且仍零化 $A$ 的多项式，矛盾；故 $m_1=m_2$。

整除性：对任意零化多项式 $f$，作带余除法 $$f(\lambda)=q(\lambda)m_A(\lambda)+r(\lambda),\qquad \deg r<\deg m_A.$$ 代入 $A$ 得 $r(A)=f(A)-q(A)m_A(A)=O$。若 $r\neq0$，它就是一个次数更低的零化多项式，与最小性矛盾；故 $r=0$，即 $m_A\mid f$。特别地 $$m_A(\lambda)\mid f_A(\lambda).$$ 方向不能反：最小多项式整除特征多项式，而不是反过来。

根集相同。若 $m_A(\lambda_0)=0$，写 $m_A=(\lambda-\lambda_0)g$，则 $$O=m_A(A)=(A-\lambda_0E)g(A).$$ 若 $\lambda_0$ 不是特征值，$A-\lambda_0E$ 可逆，左乘其逆得 $g(A)=O$，而 $\deg g<\deg m_A$，矛盾；故 $\lambda_0$ 是特征值。反之，若 $A\alpha=\lambda_0\alpha$，$\alpha\neq0$，则 $$0=m_A(A)\alpha=m_A(\lambda_0)\alpha,$$ 故 $m_A(\lambda_0)=0$。所以 $m_A$ 的根恰为 $A$ 的全部特征值，且不计重数。

重数的含义：对若尔当块 $J_k(\lambda_0)=\lambda_0E+N$，有 $(J_k-\lambda_0E)^k=N^k=O$，而 $(J_k-\lambda_0E)^{k-1}=N^{k-1}\neq O$，故 $m_{J_k}=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^k$。分块对角阵的最小多项式是各块最小多项式的最小公倍式，因为一个多项式零化整个矩阵当且仅当它零化每个块。因此 $$m_A(\lambda)=\prod_{\lambda_0}(\lambda-\lambda_0)^{k_{\max}(\lambda_0)},$$ 其中 $k_{\max}(\lambda_0)$ 是以 $\lambda_0$ 为特征值的最大若尔当块的阶。由于 $k_{\max}\le m_{\lambda_0}$（代数重数），这直接给出 $m_A\mid f_A$。

可对角化判据：由第 4 步，$$A\ \text{可对角化}\iff\text{所有若尔当块为 }1\text{ 阶}\iff k_{\max}(\lambda_0)=1\ (\forall\lambda_0).$$ 这等价于 $$m_A(\lambda)=\prod_{i=1}^s(\lambda-\lambda_i),$$ 其中 $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$ 是全部互异特征值，即 $m_A$ 在 $\mathbb{C}$ 上无重根。两个方向都成立：若 $m_A$ 无重根，则每个 $k_{\max}=1$；反之若可对角化，则每个块为 $1$ 阶，$m_A$ 就是上述互异一次因式之积。

例：$A=\operatorname{diag}\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix},5\right)$。$f_A=(\lambda-2)^2(\lambda-5)$；块 $J_2(2)$ 的最小多项式为 $(\lambda-2)^2$，块 $(5)$ 的为 $\lambda-5$，故 $$m_A=\operatorname{lcm}\bigl((\lambda-2)^2,\lambda-5\bigr)=(\lambda-2)^2(\lambda-5).$$ 它有重根 $2$，故 $A$ 不可对角化。对照 $D=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,5)$：$m_D=(\lambda-2)(\lambda-5)$ 无重根，$D$ 可对角化。还要注意，最小多项式相同不保证相似：$\operatorname{diag}(2,2,5)$ 与 $\operatorname{diag}(2,5,5)$ 的 $m$ 都是 $(\lambda-2)(\lambda-5)$，但特征多项式不同，故不相似。
en: Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb{K})$. A nonzero polynomial $f$ with $f(A)=O$ is called an annihilating polynomial of $A$. By the Cayley–Hamilton theorem the characteristic polynomial $f_A$ annihilates $A$, so annihilating polynomials exist. Among them, take the monic one of least degree; it is denoted $m_A$ and called the minimal polynomial. Uniqueness: if monic $m_1,m_2$ both have minimal degree and $m_1\neq m_2$, then $m_1-m_2$ has its leading terms cancelled, is nonzero, has lower degree and still annihilates $A$, a contradiction; hence $m_1=m_2$.

Divisibility: for any annihilating polynomial $f$, divide with remainder: $$f(\lambda)=q(\lambda)m_A(\lambda)+r(\lambda),\qquad \deg r<\deg m_A.$$ Substituting $A$ gives $r(A)=f(A)-q(A)m_A(A)=O$. If $r\neq0$, it would be an annihilating polynomial of lower degree, contradicting minimality; hence $r=0$ and $m_A\mid f$. In particular $$m_A(\lambda)\mid f_A(\lambda).$$ The direction matters: it is the minimal polynomial that divides the characteristic polynomial, not the reverse.

The roots coincide. If $m_A(\lambda_0)=0$, write $m_A=(\lambda-\lambda_0)g$; then $$O=m_A(A)=(A-\lambda_0E)g(A).$$ If $\lambda_0$ were not an eigenvalue, $A-\lambda_0E$ would be invertible, and multiplying on the left by its inverse would give $g(A)=O$ with $\deg g<\deg m_A$, a contradiction; so $\lambda_0$ is an eigenvalue. Conversely, if $A\alpha=\lambda_0\alpha$ with $\alpha\neq0$, then $$0=m_A(A)\alpha=m_A(\lambda_0)\alpha,$$ so $m_A(\lambda_0)=0$. Thus the roots of $m_A$ are exactly the eigenvalues of $A$, without multiplicity.

Meaning of multiplicity: for a Jordan block $J_k(\lambda_0)=\lambda_0E+N$, $(J_k-\lambda_0E)^k=N^k=O$ while $(J_k-\lambda_0E)^{k-1}=N^{k-1}\neq O$, so $m_{J_k}=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^k$. The minimal polynomial of a block diagonal matrix is the least common multiple of the blocks' minimal polynomials, since a polynomial annihilates the whole matrix exactly when it annihilates every block. Hence $$m_A(\lambda)=\prod_{\lambda_0}(\lambda-\lambda_0)^{k_{\max}(\lambda_0)},$$ where $k_{\max}(\lambda_0)$ is the size of the largest Jordan block with eigenvalue $\lambda_0$. Since $k_{\max}\le m_{\lambda_0}$, the algebraic multiplicity, this immediately gives $m_A\mid f_A$.

Diagonalizability criterion: by Step 4, $$A\ \text{is diagonalizable}\iff\text{all Jordan blocks have order }1\iff k_{\max}(\lambda_0)=1\ (\forall\lambda_0).$$ This is equivalent to $$m_A(\lambda)=\prod_{i=1}^s(\lambda-\lambda_i),$$ where $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s$ are all distinct eigenvalues, i.e. $m_A$ has no repeated roots over $\mathbb{C}$. Both directions hold: if $m_A$ has no repeated roots then every $k_{\max}=1$; conversely, if $A$ is diagonalizable then every block has order $1$ and $m_A$ is exactly the product of these distinct linear factors.

Example: $A=\operatorname{diag}\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix},5\right)$. Then $f_A=(\lambda-2)^2(\lambda-5)$; the block $J_2(2)$ has minimal polynomial $(\lambda-2)^2$ and the block $(5)$ has $\lambda-5$, so $$m_A=\operatorname{lcm}\bigl((\lambda-2)^2,\lambda-5\bigr)=(\lambda-2)^2(\lambda-5).$$ It has the repeated root $2$, so $A$ is not diagonalizable. By contrast, $D=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,5)$ has $m_D=(\lambda-2)(\lambda-5)$, which has no repeated root, so $D$ is diagonalizable. Note also that equal minimal polynomials do not imply similarity: $\operatorname{diag}(2,2,5)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(2,5,5)$ both have $m=(\lambda-2)(\lambda-5)$, but their characteristic polynomials differ, so they are not similar.

zh: 元素为多项式的矩阵称为 $\lambda$-矩阵，最重要的例子是方阵 $A$ 的特征矩阵 $\lambda E-A$。$\lambda$-矩阵有三类初等变换：交换两行（列）；用非零常数乘一行（列）；把一行（列）的 $\varphi(\lambda)$ 倍加到另一行（列），其中 $\varphi\in\mathbb{K}[\lambda]$。第三类允许多项式倍，这是与数字矩阵初等变换的关键差别。这些变换都可由初等矩阵实现，其逆仍是同类初等矩阵，故可逆；能互相转化的 $\lambda$-矩阵称为等价的。

Smith 标准形：设 $A(\lambda)$ 的秩为 $r$（在有理函数域 $\mathbb{K}(\lambda)$ 上取秩）。存在等价变换使 $$A(\lambda)\sim\operatorname{diag}(d_1(\lambda),\dots,d_r(\lambda),0,\dots,0),$$ 其中 $d_i$ 首一且 $d_1\mid d_2\mid\cdots\mid d_r$。存在性可用欧几里得算法：先把第一行或第一列中次数最低的非零元素移到 $(1,1)$；若 $(1,1)$ 不能整除第一行或第一列某元素，用带余除法把余式换到 $(1,1)$，使其次数下降；若余下子矩阵有元素不被 $(1,1)$ 整除，把该元素所在的行加到第一行再重复。经有限步后 $(1,1)$ 整除全部元素，用它消去第一行、第一列，再对余下的子矩阵归纳。

行列式因子与不变因子：设 $D_k(\lambda)$ 为 $A(\lambda)$ 的全部 $k$ 阶子式的首一最大公因式，约定 $D_0=1$。初等变换不改变 $D_k$：交换行（列）只改变子式的符号或位置；乘非零常数把子式乘非零常数；把一行的 $\varphi$ 倍加到另一行，子式或不变，或变成两个子式的线性组合。因此这些子式的公因式集合不变，首一 gcd 不变。对 Smith 形，当 $k\le r$ 时 $k$ 阶子式的首一 gcd 为 $d_1\cdots d_k$（这里用到整除链），故 $$D_k=d_1\cdots d_k,\qquad d_k=\frac{D_k}{D_{k-1}}.$$ 于是 Smith 形由 $D_k$ 唯一确定，两个 $\lambda$-矩阵等价当且仅当它们有相同的 $D_k$，当且仅当有相同的不变因子。

对 $n$ 阶方阵 $A$，特征矩阵 $M(\lambda)=\lambda E-A$ 的 $n$ 阶子式只有 $|M(\lambda)|=f_A(\lambda)$，故 $D_n=f_A$，从而 $$f_A=d_1d_2\cdots d_n.$$ 标准定理给出 $$m_A(\lambda)=d_n(\lambda),$$ 即最大不变因子就是最小多项式（可由 Smith 形或有理标准形证明）。于是 $d_1=\cdots=d_{n-1}=1$ 当且仅当 $m_A=f_A$，此时称 $A$ 为非亏损矩阵。这条定理把最小多项式、特征多项式与不变因子统一在同一套不变量中。

初等因子与若尔当块：把每个次数大于零的不变因子在 $\mathbb{C}$ 上分解为 $(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$ 的方幂，所有出现的这些方幂（计重数）称为初等因子。单个若尔当块 $J_m(\lambda_0)$ 的特征矩阵满足 $D_{m-1}=1$、$D_m=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$，因为取第 $1$ 至 $m-1$ 行、第 $2$ 至 $m$ 列所得的 $(m-1)$ 阶子式为非零常数 $(-1)^{m-1}$。因此每个初等因子 $(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$ 恰好对应一个 $m$ 阶若尔当块；反过来，若尔当形的初等因子就是各块对应的这些方幂。

相似分类：$$A\sim B\iff \lambda E-A\cong\lambda E-B\iff\text{初等因子组相同}.$$ 若 $B=P^{-1}AP$，则 $\lambda E-B=P^{-1}(\lambda E-A)P$，常数可逆矩阵是幺模的，故特征矩阵等价。反之，若两特征矩阵等价，则它们有相同的初等因子；第 5 步说明初等因子组唯一确定若尔当形（不计块序），而每个矩阵都相似于自己的若尔当形，故 $A\sim B$。例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$，$M(\lambda)=\lambda E-A$ 有 $D_1=1$（含非零常数 $-1$）；二阶子式含 $(\lambda-1)^2$ 与 $-(\lambda-2)$，二者互素，故 $D_2=1$；$D_3=(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda-2)$。于是 $$d_1=d_2=1,\quad d_3=(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda-2),$$ 初等因子为 $(\lambda-1)^2,\lambda-2$，对应 $J_2(1)\oplus J_1(2)$，恰为原矩阵；$m_A=d_3$。可对角化当且仅当所有初等因子都是一次式。
en: A matrix whose entries are polynomials is called a $\lambda$-matrix; the most important example is the characteristic matrix $\lambda E-A$ of a square matrix $A$. There are three kinds of elementary transformations: interchange two rows (columns); multiply a row (column) by a nonzero constant; add a polynomial multiple $\varphi(\lambda)$ of one row (column) to another, where $\varphi\in\mathbb{K}[\lambda]$. The third type allows polynomial multipliers, a key difference from elementary transformations of constant matrices. Each transformation is implemented by an elementary matrix whose inverse is again of the same type, hence is invertible; two $\lambda$-matrices related by such transformations are called equivalent.

Smith normal form: let $r$ be the rank of $A(\lambda)$ over the rational function field $\mathbb{K}(\lambda)$. Then $A(\lambda)$ is equivalent to $$A(\lambda)\sim\operatorname{diag}(d_1(\lambda),\dots,d_r(\lambda),0,\dots,0),$$ where the $d_i$ are monic and $d_1\mid d_2\mid\cdots\mid d_r$. Existence follows from the Euclidean algorithm: first move a nonzero entry of least degree in the first row or column to position $(1,1)$; if $(1,1)$ does not divide some entry in the first row or column, division with remainder moves a lower-degree remainder into $(1,1)$; if some entry of the remaining submatrix is not divisible by $(1,1)$, add its row to the first row and repeat. After finitely many steps $(1,1)$ divides every entry, so it can clear the first row and column, and one proceeds inductively on the remaining submatrix.

Determinantal divisors and invariant factors: let $D_k(\lambda)$ be the monic greatest common divisor of all $k\times k$ minors of $A(\lambda)$, with $D_0=1$. Elementary transformations preserve $D_k$: interchanging rows (columns) only changes signs or positions of minors; multiplying by a nonzero constant multiplies minors by a nonzero constant; adding a $\varphi$-multiple of one row to another either leaves a minor unchanged or replaces it by a linear combination of two minors. Hence the common-divisor set, and therefore the monic gcd, is unchanged. For the Smith form, when $k\le r$ the monic gcd of the $k\times k$ minors is $d_1\cdots d_k$ (using the divisibility chain), so $$D_k=d_1\cdots d_k,\qquad d_k=\frac{D_k}{D_{k-1}}.$$ Thus the Smith form is determined by the $D_k$, and two $\lambda$-matrices are equivalent iff they have the same $D_k$, iff they have the same invariant factors.

For an $n\times n$ matrix $A$, the characteristic matrix $M(\lambda)=\lambda E-A$ has only one $n\times n$ minor, $|M(\lambda)|=f_A(\lambda)$, so $D_n=f_A$ and $$f_A=d_1d_2\cdots d_n.$$ A standard theorem gives $$m_A(\lambda)=d_n(\lambda),$$ i.e. the largest invariant factor is the minimal polynomial (this can be proved from the Smith form or from rational canonical form). Consequently $d_1=\cdots=d_{n-1}=1$ iff $m_A=f_A$, in which case $A$ is called non-derogatory. This theorem unifies the minimal polynomial, the characteristic polynomial and the invariant factors in one set of invariants.

Elementary divisors and Jordan blocks: factor every invariant factor of positive degree over $\mathbb{C}$ into powers $(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$; all such powers, counted with multiplicity, are the elementary divisors. For a single Jordan block $J_m(\lambda_0)$, the characteristic matrix has $D_{m-1}=1$ and $D_m=(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$, because the $(m-1)\times(m-1)$ minor formed by rows $1,\dots,m-1$ and columns $2,\dots,m$ is the nonzero constant $(-1)^{m-1}$. Therefore each elementary divisor $(\lambda-\lambda_0)^m$ corresponds to exactly one Jordan block of order $m$, and conversely the elementary divisors of a Jordan form are precisely the powers attached to its blocks.

Similarity classification: $$A\sim B\iff \lambda E-A\cong\lambda E-B\iff\text{the elementary divisors agree}.$$ If $B=P^{-1}AP$, then $\lambda E-B=P^{-1}(\lambda E-A)P$, and a constant invertible matrix is unimodular, so the characteristic matrices are equivalent. Conversely, equivalent characteristic matrices have the same elementary divisors; by Step 5 these determine the Jordan form up to order, and every matrix is similar to its Jordan form, so $A\sim B$. Example: $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$; for $M(\lambda)=\lambda E-A$, $D_1=1$ (the entry $-1$ is a nonzero constant); the $2\times2$ minors include $(\lambda-1)^2$ and $-(\lambda-2)$, which are coprime, so $D_2=1$; and $D_3=(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda-2)$. Hence $$d_1=d_2=1,\quad d_3=(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda-2),$$ with elementary divisors $(\lambda-1)^2,\lambda-2$, corresponding to $J_2(1)\oplus J_1(2)$, which is exactly the original matrix; also $m_A=d_3$. A matrix is diagonalizable iff all elementary divisors are linear.

zh: 在 $\mathbb{C}^n$ 上取内积 $(\alpha,\beta)=\beta^H\alpha$，其中 $A^H=\bar A^T$。若 $$A^HA=AA^H,$$ 称 $A$ 为正规矩阵。Hermitian 矩阵（$A^H=A$）、斜 Hermitian 矩阵（$A^H=-A$）与酉矩阵（$U^HU=E$）都是正规矩阵：前两者 $A^HA$ 与 $AA^H$ 都等于 $A^2$ 或 $-A^2$，酉矩阵两者都等于 $E$。因此正规类是这三类矩阵的共同推广。

范数刻画：$$\|Ax\|^2=x^HA^HAx,\qquad \|A^Hx\|^2=x^HAA^Hx.$$ 令 $B=A^HA-AA^H$，则 $B^H=B$，且 $$\|Ax\|^2-\|A^Hx\|^2=x^HBx.$$ 若 $A$ 正规，$B=0$，两范数相等。反之，若对一切 $x$ 有 $x^HBx=0$，由 Hermitian 形式的极化恒等式 $$y^HBx=\frac14\sum_{k=0}^{3}i^k(x+i^ky)^HB(x+i^ky)$$ 得 $y^HBx=0$ 对一切 $x,y$ 成立。取 $y=Bx$，则 $\|Bx\|^2=(Bx)^HBx=0$，故 $Bx=0$；由 $x$ 任意得 $B=0$，即 $A^HA=AA^H$。所以正规性等价于 $\|Ax\|=\|A^Hx\|$ 对一切 $x$ 成立。

一个方向（酉对角化 $\Rightarrow$ 正规）：设 $A=U\Lambda U^H$，$U^HU=E$，$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$。则 $A^H=U\bar\Lambda U^H$，于是 $$A^HA=U\bar\Lambda\Lambda U^H,\qquad AA^H=U\Lambda\bar\Lambda U^H.$$ 对角矩阵相乘可交换，$\bar\Lambda\Lambda=\Lambda\bar\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(|\lambda_i|^2)$，故 $A^HA=AA^H$，即 $A$ 正规。此时 $U$ 的列就是标准正交特征向量，$Au_i=\lambda_i u_i$。

反方向（正规 $\Rightarrow$ 酉对角化）：由 Schur 三角化，任意复方阵可写 $A=UTU^H$，$U$ 酉、$T$ 上三角，对角元为特征值。酉相似保持正规性：$$T^HT=U^HA^HAU,\qquad TT^H=U^HAA^HU,$$ 故 $T$ 正规。比较 $T^HT$ 与 $TT^H$ 的 $(1,1)$ 元：左端为 $|t_{11}|^2$（第一列只有 $t_{11}$），右端为 $\sum_{j=1}^n|t_{1j}|^2$，故 $t_{12}=\cdots=t_{1n}=0$。于是第一行只剩 $t_{11}$；对从第 $2$ 行第 $2$ 列起的子块重复同样论证，依次得 $t_{23}=\cdots=t_{2n}=0$、……，最终 $T$ 为对角阵。因此 $A=UTU^H$ 可酉对角化。

推论：正规矩阵属于不同特征值的特征向量正交。设 $Ax=\lambda x$，$Ay=\mu y$，$x,y
eq0$，$\lambda
eq\mu$。$A-\mu E$ 仍正规，由第 2 步 $$ igl\|(A-\mu E)^Hy igr\|= igl\|(A-\mu E)y igr\|=0,$$ 故 $A^Hy= ar\mu y$。于是 $$\lambda(x,y)=(Ax,y)=(x,A^Hy)=\mu(x,y),$$ 即 $(\lambda-\mu)(x,y)=0$；由于 $\lambda
eq\mu$，得 $(x,y)=0$。这说明正规矩阵的特征子空间两两正交，必要时只需在各子空间内部标准正交化。

特殊谱：Hermitian 矩阵满足 $$\lambda\|x\|^2=(Ax,x)=x^HAx\in\mathbb{R},$$ 故 $\lambda=\bar\lambda$；斜 Hermitian 矩阵满足 $x^HAx=-(Ax)^Hx=-\bar\lambda\|x\|^2$，故 $\lambda=-\bar\lambda$，即特征值为纯虚数；酉矩阵满足 $\|Ux\|=\|x\|$，故 $|\lambda|=1$。实对称矩阵是 Hermitian 的实特例，可正交对角化；一般实正规矩阵只能正交化为块对角形，非实特征值成共轭对，对应 $2\times2$ 旋转—伸缩块。反例：$B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ 特征值 $1,2$ 互异，故可对角化，但 $$B^TB=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&5\end{pmatrix}\neq\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}=BB^T,$$ 故 $B$ 不正规，不能酉对角化。
en: On $\mathbb{C}^n$ use the inner product $(\alpha,\beta)=\beta^H\alpha$, where $A^H=\bar A^T$. A matrix $A$ is normal if $$A^HA=AA^H.$$ Hermitian matrices ($A^H=A$), skew-Hermitian matrices ($A^H=-A$) and unitary matrices ($U^HU=E$) are all normal: for the first two, both $A^HA$ and $AA^H$ equal $A^2$ or $-A^2$; for a unitary matrix both equal $E$. Thus normal matrices form a common generalization of these three classes.

Norm characterization: $$\|Ax\|^2=x^HA^HAx,\qquad \|A^Hx\|^2=x^HAA^Hx.$$ Let $B=A^HA-AA^H$; then $B^H=B$ and $$\|Ax\|^2-\|A^Hx\|^2=x^HBx.$$ If $A$ is normal, $B=0$ and the two norms are equal. Conversely, if $x^HBx=0$ for every $x$, the polarization identity for Hermitian forms $$y^HBx=\frac14\sum_{k=0}^{3}i^k(x+i^ky)^HB(x+i^ky)$$ gives $y^HBx=0$ for all $x,y$. Taking $y=Bx$ yields $\|Bx\|^2=(Bx)^HBx=0$, so $Bx=0$ for every $x$, hence $B=0$, i.e. $A^HA=AA^H$. Thus normality is equivalent to $\|Ax\|=\|A^Hx\|$ for all $x$.

One direction (unitary diagonalization $\Rightarrow$ normal): let $A=U\Lambda U^H$ with $U^HU=E$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$. Then $A^H=U\bar\Lambda U^H$, so $$A^HA=U\bar\Lambda\Lambda U^H,\qquad AA^H=U\Lambda\bar\Lambda U^H.$$ Diagonal matrices commute, and $\bar\Lambda\Lambda=\Lambda\bar\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(|\lambda_i|^2)$, so $A^HA=AA^H$ and $A$ is normal. In this case the columns of $U$ are orthonormal eigenvectors, $Au_i=\lambda_i u_i$.

Converse (normal $\Rightarrow$ unitarily diagonalizable): by Schur triangularization every complex matrix can be written $A=UTU^H$ with $U$ unitary and $T$ upper triangular whose diagonal entries are the eigenvalues. Unitary similarity preserves normality: $$T^HT=U^HA^HAU,\qquad TT^H=U^HAA^HU,$$ so $T$ is normal. Compare the $(1,1)$ entries of $T^HT$ and $TT^H$: the left side is $|t_{11}|^2$ (the first column has only $t_{11}$), while the right side is $\sum_{j=1}^n|t_{1j}|^2$; hence $t_{12}=\cdots=t_{1n}=0$. Thus the first row has only $t_{11}$; applying the same argument to the submatrix starting at row $2$, column $2$ (where $t_{12}=0$ ensures the second column has only $t_{22}$) gives $t_{23}=\cdots=t_{2n}=0$, and so on, until $T$ is diagonal. Therefore $A=UTU^H$ is unitarily diagonalizable.

Corollary: eigenvectors of a normal matrix belonging to distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal. Let $Ax=\lambda x$ and $Ay=\mu y$ with $x,y
eq0$ and $\lambda
eq\mu$. Since $A-\mu E$ is still normal, Step 2 gives $$ igl\|(A-\mu E)^Hy igr\|= igl\|(A-\mu E)y igr\|=0,$$ so $A^Hy= ar\mu y$. Therefore $$\lambda(x,y)=(Ax,y)=(x,A^Hy)=\mu(x,y),$$ i.e. $(\lambda-\mu)(x,y)=0$; since $\lambda
eq\mu$, $(x,y)=0$. Thus the eigenspaces of a normal matrix are mutually orthogonal, and orthonormalization is needed only inside each eigenspace.

Special spectra: for Hermitian $A$, $$\lambda\|x\|^2=(Ax,x)=x^HAx\in\mathbb{R},$$ so $\lambda=\bar\lambda$; for skew-Hermitian $A$, $x^HAx=-(Ax)^Hx=-\bar\lambda\|x\|^2$, so $\lambda=-\bar\lambda$, i.e. eigenvalues are purely imaginary; for unitary $A$, $\|Ux\|=\|x\|$ gives $|\lambda|=1$. A real symmetric matrix is the real Hermitian case and is orthogonally diagonalizable; a general real normal matrix can only be orthogonally reduced to block diagonal form, nonreal eigenvalues occurring in conjugate pairs and corresponding to $2\times2$ rotation-dilation blocks. Counterexample: $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ has distinct eigenvalues $1,2$, hence is diagonalizable, but $$B^TB=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&5\end{pmatrix}\neq\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}=BB^T,$$ so $B$ is not normal and cannot be unitarily diagonalized.
